newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold buoyed by physical demand.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold buoyed by physical demand.

text.p: Strong demand for physical gold in Hong Kong supported the spot price at about US$381.00 on Monday despite overseas selling interest, gold dealers said.
"We saw a lot of physical buying interest as the price of gold has dropped," said a source at a local bank.
The tightness in Hong Kong's supply of kilobars has begun to ease as fresh supplies have reached the market and more are expected during the week, industry sources said.
"As a result, premiums on gold have softened slightly by about HK$1 per tael or about US cents 10 per ounce," said the chief bullion dealer at another bank in the territory.

The territory saw some speculative selling from Europe on bearish market sentiment, gold traders said, with one industry source still pointing to the lack of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) decision on gold sales last Wednesday.
"People were selling gold mainly because of weakness in silver," another gold source noted.
Bullion ended at US$381.00/381.50 an ounce Monday against New York's US$380.85/381.35 close on Friday.
Local gold ended unchanged at HK$3,512 a tael. The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society on Monday remained unchanged from its Friday fix at -6.
"When spot prices go down, it is quite normal for players (on the Exchange) to try and get rid of their long positions," another gold trader said.
